The accompanying source-level functional change is the BYOK reasoning-effort feature (member 41c03830), implemented across `cli/src/commands/byok.ts`, `cli/src/utils/byok.ts`, `cli/src/utils/settings.ts`, `common/src/constants/reasoning-effort.ts`, `sdk/src/byok.ts`, `sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts`, and `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, which adds a `/byok effort` command and per-provider request-body translation so a BYOK run can request low/medium/high reasoning effort, persisted as `byokReasoningEffort` and retried once without the field if rejected.

Added a /byok effort command and per-connection reasoning-effort attachment with per-provider request translation and one-time field-stripping retry on rejection.
Added freebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval, freebuffSubscriptionMrrUsd, and the SubscriptionBillingIntervals aggregate type for billing-cadence MRR reporting.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.10 lets you pick how much 'thinking' a BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) run does, per run, instead of leaving it to the provider's default. You can choose low, medium, or high reasoning effort with a new `/byok effort` command, and that choice is saved in your settings and applied only to the BYOK connection you selected. The pick is translated into the right request field for each provider: OpenRouter gets a `reasoning.effort` value, Anthropic gets a thinking budget added to its max output tokens, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints (including Gemini and most others) get a `reasoning_effort` value. If a provider or model rejects that field with a 400 error naming it, the run automatically retries once without it, and that refusal is remembered for that specific connection so later steps in the same run do not ask again. Editing the connection later (which changes its revision) resets that memory, so a changed connection gets a fresh chance at the request field. Also in this release, the Freebuff subscription catalog and admin cost-reporting tooling now split paying subscribers by monthly and yearly billing cadence, counting a yearly plan as one-twelfth of its annual price for MRR reporting, though these are backend operator/admin changes rather than new user-facing subscription options. The release also bumps the shipped package version from 0.1.9 to 0.1.10.

ai.title: Guard against file edits cut off mid-generation
ai.summary: A new `truncated-write-guard.ts` module in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util` refuses two shapes of a file edit cut off mid-generation. Both refusals log the new `FILE_WRITE_GUARD_EVENT` to Axiom via the allowlist added in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, and the change adds tests and a docs section describing the guard.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.11 release bump
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped from `0.1.10` to `0.1.11`. This release packages the truncated-write guard shipped in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/truncated-write-guard.ts` and wired through `processFileBlock` and `tool-executor.ts`, which refuses file edits cut off mid-generation and logs `file_write_guard` to Axiom via `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`. The version field is the only source change in this commit; the functional guard itself landed in the earlier member commit.
ai.evidence: The diff bumps the version field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` from `0.1.10` to `0.1.11`; the Analysis notes state this is the Freebuff CLI release 0.1.11 published, and the same-day commit sequence places it after the 0.1.10 BYOK release and the truncated-write guard work.

eli5.text: This release adds a safety check that stops the assistant from saving a file when its output gets cut off mid-sentence. New files: a guard module in the agent runtime, an allowlisted telemetry event (file_write_guard) so refusals are recorded in Axiom with only content-free details, plus docs and tests. Concrete changes: when a tool call's arguments are incomplete (a JSON prefix that never closes, like an unclosed string or bracket), the runtime now returns an explicit 'nothing was written' error instead of the generic retry hint, and does not echo the partial text back; and when a write_file would replace an existing file of 30+ lines with a copy under 60% of its size that leaves brackets open where the current file balances them, processFileBlock refuses the write and logs file_write_guard/truncated_rewrite_refused. Everyday impact: if your session hits the output limit or the connection drops while the assistant is writing a file, the file on disk is left unchanged and you are told the call was refused, rather than receiving a truncated half-written file; you are guided to use smaller str_replace edits or to resend complete content. Tests assert the two refusal shapes and the telemetry allowlist, confirming the guard is wired in, though telemetry visibility itself depends on operator settings for Axiom. No other features, models, or billing changes are established by the evidence; the available release evidence is complete only for this truncated-write guard.

ai.title: Freebuff auth token moved to OS keychain at startup
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now loads the bearer token from the OS credential store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service) via Bun.secrets before anything reads credentials. cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts is the new store module exposing bunSecretStore, getCachedKeychainToken, setCachedKeychainToken, moveTokenToKeychain, loadStoredAuthToken and resolveSecretStore, with KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000 bounding every keychain call. cli/src/index.tsx calls await loadStoredAuthToken() during startup, and cli/src/utils/auth.ts migrates existing installs: saveUserCredentials moves the file token into the keychain, clearUserCredentials deletes the keychain item too, and a keychain-pointer profile (tokenStore: 'keychain', no authToken) reads the token from the in-memory cache instead of the file. The file keeps the profile and stays owner-only, so a failed or unavailable keychain leaves the token in the file without logging anyone out.

eli5.text: The Freebuff CLI now saves your login token in your operating system's built-in password manager (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service) when you launch it, instead of leaving it in a plain text file on your computer. This is live today for Freebuff users. You should notice nothing different beyond the first launch, which silently moves your existing token into the OS password store; the local file stays as a backup, so if the password manager can't be reached (for example on a headless server or over SSH), you stay logged in normally.
